newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes strong on Greenspan testimony.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes strong on Greenspan testimony.

text.p: The Mexican peso gained substantial ground from the dollar at the close of trade on Tuesday following a dip in U.S. long bond yields following testimony by Alan Greenspan to a U.S. Congress panel, dealers said.
"Dealers went short on dollars on the expectation U.S. interest rates will not rise this year," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed trade 4.7 and 4.5 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8380/7.8410 and 7.8350/7.8400 per dollar.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were up 43/32 to yield 6.44 percent in late trade following comments by Greenspan that "for the present, demand growth does appear to have moderated."
Dealers said they took the comment to mean gains in U.S. interest rates were not imminent.

"The market had been expecting bad news from Greenspan and the opposite happened; (U.S.) long bond yields dropped and everyone rushed to sell dollars," another dealer said. Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 2.9 centavos firmer at 7.8470/7.8510 per dollar.
